concerns.text: T012 describes handling duplicates by 'retaining most recent assay date' but omits the FR-009 requirement to 'average the conflicting experimental values if dates match'. This is a semantic weakening of the deduplication logic, risking data leakage or incorrect aggregation.

T013 implements a memory-safety halving strategy but fails to mandate logging the final sample size and the number of reduction iterations. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and SC-005 (Resource Conformance) by omitting the audit trail required to verify the dataset size cap was reached deterministically.

T009 mandates recording the checksum to `state/...yaml` but does not explicitly require the task to fail if the checksum file (`chembl_33.sha256`) is missing from the FTP directory. Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) requires checksumming; a missing checksum file should trigger a hard failure, not a silent skip or mock.

T034 (Resource Gate) is blocked by T018/T019 (Model Training). This creates a circular dependency where the mandatory resource constraint verification (Constitution Principle VII) cannot run until the models it is meant to constrain are already trained. The task must be re-architected to run on the data pipeline alone or as a pre-flight check.
